chunks: These are only names which you and your fathers have invented. No authority was sent down by God for them. They only follow conjecture and wish-fulfilment, even though guidance had come to them already from their Lord.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the basis of idol worship and ancestral tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to critique *taqlid* (blind imitation) of ancestral traditions when lacking scriptural proof, emphasizing that idolatry stems from following mere conjecture (*zann*) and base desires (*hawā*) rather than divine revelation. It underscores the sufficiency of the guidance already provided by Allah, rendering human-made deities invalid as they possess no *sultān* (authority) or revealed basis.
